  • Top administration officials doubled down on calls for Congress to supply additional funds for an ongoing air traffic modernization effort after they noted old equipment contributed to the need for a nationwide ground stop of flights on Friday.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin increased their ask to $50 billion on Friday night, a day after Duffy and White House budget chief Russ Vought formally requested $30.1 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy leaves a House Republican Conference meeting in the Capitol on July 21. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Top administration officials doubled down on calls for Congress to supply additional funds for an ongoing air traffic modernization effort after they noted old equipment contributed to the need for a nationwide ground stop of flights on Friday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin increased their ask to $50 billion on Friday night, a day after Duffy and White House budget chief Russ Vought formally requested $30.1 billion.

The increased allotment, which the administration officials didn’t fully flesh out, comes after the nation’s air traffic control system experienced “instability” in its radar and communications at certain facilities earlier in the day, Duffy told reporters.

He mentioned “inconsistency in the data” being issued by those systems led to implementation of the nationwide ground stop, saying the order was given out of “an abundance of caution” before being lifted about four hours later.

During a Friday night White House briefing, Duffy and Mullin explained the issues were driven by “an incredibly old air traffic control system.”.

Earlier in the day, the stoppage had caused mass confusion and raised questions about potential terror attacks, or artificial intelligence breakouts resulting from new software the agency is rolling out. While Mullin said “we’re not ruling out anything,” he explained that “the public was never at danger through this process.”.

Still, Duffy called the incident “an emergency” while calling for additional modernization funds.

Recent findings suggest that “This is an emergency,” he said. “I want $50 billion. President Trump is a builder. He’s going to build this network and deliver for the American people. But the president can’t deliver for America unless the Congress delivers the money to make it happen.”.

The latest figure is $19.1 billion higher than the figure Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought called on congressional appropriators to approve in a Thursday letter.

Mullin noted the newly introduced $50 billion figure was an administration estimate for a “complete overhaul of the system” which has been going through a “patchwork” upgrade process that may have overwhelmed the older equipment still being used.

“We need someone to come in and build the whole system," Mullin said. "Nickel and diming it together does not work.".

In a recent development, thursday’s call for $30.1 billion echoes a White House-backed bill that Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., introduced in September, which would provide $10.1 billion for air traffic control upgrades, including $2 billion for "cloud computing and national airspace system telecommunications.".

Those funds would come after $12.5 billion allocated to the effort through the July 2025 reconciliation law that Duffy and Vought called a “down-payment.".

Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee Republicans touted those already-appropriated funds in a social media post. They pointed to $1.9 billion provided in the reconciliation law that would go toward upgrading air route traffic control centers, which guide planes across long distances after departure and which the FAA had cited as the cause of the problem.

The 22 air route traffic control centers across the country guide aircraft using instrument-dependent flight prepares. Under such plans, pilots use instruments, electronic navigation and air traffic control assistance to guide them and maintain separation from other aircraft in certain airspaces.

The committee’s majority remarked Friday's outage highlighted the need to prioritize modernization of the air route traffic control centers, arguing that President Lyndon B. Johnson was in office the last time a new one was built.

Commerce ranking member Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., said in a statement Friday night that the panel is looking into FAA and airspace telecommunications issues.

“Technology issues related to how planes communicate through primary frequencies, backup frequencies, and other issues will be something the Commerce Committee will be reviewing,” Cantwell noted.

Cantwell is poised to take the committee's gavel come January as Democrats assume the majority in the Senate.

In a joint statement Friday night, House Transportation and Infrastructure Chairman Sam Graves, R-Mo., and ranking member Rick Larsen, D-Wash., called the communication failures “concerning” and stated their committee would “thoroughly review the complications that led to this nationwide ground stop.”.

Both committees have also been in monthslong negotiations over dueling aviation safety bills responding to the January 2025 midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport that killed 67 people.

At issue in those negotiations is which location transmission technology should be mandated to aid in air traffic control operations and allow aircraft to maintain appropriate distance. Leaders have said they hope to reach a deal in the lame-duck session.

Mein Schiff 3 will set sail on its first cruise following its collision in Bremerhaven with a temporary lifeboat solution, while three latest lifeboats will be delivered at a later date.

As reported by Schiffe und Kreuzfahrten, the lifeboats need to be manufactured anew after they were destroyed in a collision with a container ship at the end of October while the ship was leaving Bremerhaven in stormy conditions on its way to Spain.

Since the forward lifeboats on the starboard side, including their superstructures, have not yet been repaired, the ship will likely receive additional life rafts to ensure that there are sufficient spaces available for the unlikely event of an evacuation.

New lifeboats, which are expected to be produced over the next few months, can then be taken onboard when the ship calls at port.

At the time of the collision, the port authority stated that lifeboats, their associated cranes and the outer hull were damaged on the cruise ship during the incident.

TUI confirmed last week that the next scheduled cruise following repairs at Lloyd Wrft Bremerhaven will go ahead as planned, departing on Saturday, November 28, 2026.

Captain Günter Batzner is set to command the bridge during this first cruise to Kiel, where he will be replaced by Captain Alexander Orendt, the ship’s regular captain who is set to return following vacation.

It has been revealed that they will replace Captain Jan F. Schubert, who commanded the ship when the collision happened, as he is under investigation by the Bremen maritime police to determine whether he breached his duty of care by departing in adverse weather conditions.

Extinct, long-legged grasshoppers walked on water alongside dinosaurs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Nearly 100 million years ago, spindly legged grasshoppers may have scooted across water like modern day water striders.
  • Sources indicate that special hairs and leaf-shaped leg adornments, exquisitely preserved in amber, suggest the insects — members of a newfound family of insects — could balance and slide around on surface tension, researchers report November 24 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

Nearly 100 million years ago, spindly legged grasshoppers may have scooted across water like modern day water striders. The clues are in the fossilized insects’ legs and feet.

Sources indicate that special hairs and leaf-shaped leg adornments, exquisitely preserved in amber, suggest the insects — members of a newfound family of insects — could balance and slide around on surface tension, researchers report November 24 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The discovery suggests at least three insect groups evolved independently to move across water.

Paleontologist Chunpeng Xu and his colleagues first encountered the strange insects while studying a collection of 99-million-year-old amber. Frozen in time were three pieces of amber containing wingless grasshoppers with short bodies and incredibly long, skinny legs. Due to their unorthodox body shape, Xu didn’t recognize them as grasshoppers at first and thought they might be harvestmen or stick insects.“I was genuinely amazed,” says Xu, of the Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology in China. “They are among the most bizarre insects.”.

Under the microscope, two details stood out: Front legs with water repellant hairs and rear lower legs with leaf-shaped paddlelike structures. Estimates of the insects’ weight show they could have ridden on the water’s surface tension, with help from the repellant hairs on their legs and their spread-out footprint across the surface of the water. And the paddlelike lower legs would have propelled them forward.

The researchers named the insects Hydrelcana zhangi, placing them in the latest family Hydrelcanidae.

Sources indicate that “Walking on water is a pretty rare skill in nature,” Xu says. Until now, only two insect groups were known to have evolved to live on the water’s surface: water striders and their kin, and a similar looking but unrelated, long extinct family called Chresmodidae.

It has been revealed that the grasshoppers had a different gait from other water-walking insects. The common pond skater (Gerris lacustris), by comparison, rows with its middle limbs.

And whereas modern water-walking insects are predators and scavengers, the ancient grasshoppers were also probably herbivorous, given their mouthparts and lack of claws. The researchers found nine of them preserved in the same amber chunk, suggesting the insects may have gathered in large numbers to feed. It’s possibly the earliest record of such swarming behavior in grasshoppers or crickets, the team says.

Thomas brings communications experience to her role. As owner of Community Strategies, LLC, she provided a range of services to major energy, petrochemical and health care organizations.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that smartphones may give us an easy access to a light source, but for seeing objects at a distance or brightening a workspace in places like the attic or under the sink, you need the power and range of a LED (light-emitting diode) flashlight.
  • We’ve tested a variety of popular models to find the best flashlights, whether you’re looking for one to use in the midst of a blackout or simply want to put a decent one in the glove box of your car, just in case.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that smartphones may give us an easy access to a light source, but for seeing objects at a distance or brightening a workspace in places like the attic or under the sink, you need the power and range of a LED (light-emitting diode) flashlight. Flashlights are vital for navigating the outdoors at night and absolutely essential during a blackout or emergency, when you don’t want to drain your phone’s battery.

We’ve tested a variety of popular models to find the best flashlights, whether you’re looking for one to use in the midst of a blackout or simply want to put a decent one in the glove box of your car, just in case.

Perhaps the most notable element of testing flashlights is to ensure they’re as bright as manufacturers claim. Brands typically list a lumen count, though they’re often inflated. Flashlights tend to dim slightly after you turn them on and your eyes adjust, and how promptly they do so is key. It’s not just about the peak brightness, but how long that brightness actually lasts and how bright the light is after it dims.

It has been revealed that to measure lumen, you need an integrating sphere, which is an expensive piece of equipment. So for testing flashlights, we built our own. We consulted with product engineers at two different companies to go over our prepares. We also used their commercial spheres to verify lumens on calibration lights to make sure that our own sphere sensors would be accurate.

After construction and calibration, we measured each flashlight individually at specific time intervals. We recorded our measurements immediately after turning on the light, every 30 seconds for the first 3 minutes, at 5 minutes, and then every 5 minutes for a full half an hour. Our official figure is based on our measurement at 30 seconds because most flashlights drop brightness quickly after that before eventually stabilizing at a dimmer level.

After completing the quantitative portion of our testing process, we used each flashlight in a variety of real-world applications, noting aspects including quality of build, ergonomics, weight, water-resistance, and other key specs.

Industry observers note that our best overall is an evolution on the classic hefty Maglite you remember in your parents junk drawer that could blind you if you looked directly at it. This model trades in the D batteries for a rechargeable and replaceable battery. Furthermore, the flashlight has an LED bulb that shines just as brightly as the old-school models you remember.

While Maglite lists that the flashlight shines with a brightness of 1,082 lumens, our own testing measured an even higher figure, not dropping below 1,082 lumens for more than three minutes.

Recent findings suggest that beyond this, I really love how it feels in my hand. It isn’t quite as clunky as the giant models of the past, but it still boasts a similar heft that feels solid and durable. The aluminum frame and IPX4 water resistance rating backs that feeling up.

If raw lumens and longevity are top of your priority list, it’s hard to find a better choice than the Streamlight Polytac X USB. The starting point of 554 lumens is already solid, but in testing, the flashlight settles between 334 and 324 lumens, which is a far higher than nearly all other options we tested.

Recent findings suggest that the relatively compact design doesn’t detract from the overall performance, as the light beam extends for close to 300 feet. That remarked, the reflector is not adjustable, so you’ll have to look elsewhere for a floodlight.

Beyond this, we liked the nylon polymer body which was grippy and a lot more comfortable to hold in comparison to a fully metal exterior, which can be icy to the touch in cold temperatures.

In a recent development, there are three preprogrammed function sets we were able to access using Streamlight’s Ten-Tap selector switch. The selection process is a little awkward, but most people will likely only use it sparingly to set the preferred programs, which include low/medium/high, high/strobe/low, and high only. We recommend reading the instructions thoroughly to get this right.

From a fully charged state, the Polytac X ran for almost 5.5 hours during our runtime test before going dark.

No, Energizer isn’t just for batteries and Jeep isn’t just for cars. The collaboration between the two brands has led to an affordable, sturdy flashlight with enough brightness to cut through the darkness during late nights on the trails or on the roadside.

While Jeep’s involvement isn’t more than some design elements and a logo, this particular option is part of a larger lighting collection the brand did in collaboration with Energizer, featuring headlamps and other flashlights.

In a recent development, during our lumen testing, the flashlight measured a little less than 20 percent below the 1,000 lumens Energizer claims, which isn’t uncommon given nearly all flashlights fall a little short of their advertised number. It still offers tremendous light, especially in tandem with the reflector and lens, which do a nice job angling the light out in a steady, powerful beam.

Test Editor Bradley Ford noted: “The unique feature on this light is the Power Indicator screen for which it is named. When the light is turned on, or the mode changed, the screen displays estimated runtime for that mode—then it switches to battery capacity, listed as charge capacity remaining. Really a nice feature, and better than typical three or four battery-level indicators that are more common.”.

Sources indicate that we’ve tested other flashlights from ThruNite and were impressed by their durable, powerful lighting. That’s why we called in the Archer 2A V3 to test.

The flashlight is said to have more than 8 hours of consistent lumen output, higher than many flashlights we tested. Along with brightness, the Archer flashlight is compact and easy to carry around for everyday tasks. Need a quick light to check the back of your shed? Simply reach into your pocket and use the Archer.

In a recent development, the ThruNite won’t be top of the list in any one category but thrives on being pretty consistent across all of them. It’s bright, long-lasting, and durable, which is just about all you really need.

This ArkPro line of flashlights from Olight caught our eye not just for its slim, pocket-sized design, but also for the volume of additional features it offers. The ArkPro Ultra has four different lighting options: a long-range spotlight, a shallow floodlight, a UV light, and a laser pointer.

Recent findings suggest that furthermore, you can use those lights in combination with one another. For example, you can turn the laser pointer on and off while shining the flood.

During testing, the long-range spotlight and floodlight ended up being our favorite dual feature. We were able to illuminate small dark rooms easily with the shallow floodlight, while using the long-range spotlight for hallways and large empty spaces. Having both in one body is not a common feature. While we might have initially winced at the price tag, the Olight makes a solid case that it has the value of multiple flashlights.

That mentioned, it’s worth noting that our measured lumens fell short of Olight’s claimed 1,700 figure. The flashlight is still much brighter than most other options but did degrade over the 30-minute test.

Another promising feature: the physical display lights on the body that indicate battery, brightness, and a lockout mode. That last one prevents kids from accidentally flashing the laser or other lights in their eyes by locking the device from shutting on and off.

It has been revealed that the USB-C charging is also a plus. With nearly every smartphone charger already built in the same design, you’ve likely got dozens of compatible charging cords lying around.

Full Olight ArkPro Ultra Review.

In a recent development, this small, tactical flashlight from ThruNite does a number of key things well. The over 2400 lumens at its brightest setting rivals some of the most powerful options we recommend. At the same time the compact body and hip clip make it a great portable option that easily slips in a pocket or center console of your car.

What sets the TC15 apart from other options is the extraordinary runtime. On its Firefly mode (which is admittedly a very low setting), the flashlight can run for up to 30 days before needing to recharge.

The durable aluminum body is capable of handling a steep drop and the IPX8 rating means you can feel confident using it in the rain.

It has been revealed that traditional light bulbs, while nostalgic, are inefficient and waste a lot of energy. According to the U.S. Department of Energy, as much as 90 percent of the energy required to illuminate an incandescent light is given off—essentially lost—as heat. Halogen bulbs are an improvement on classic incandescent lights, but still generate a ton of heat. Beyond this, the bulbs themselves are also quite delicate. If dropped, they can easily shatter.

In contrast, LEDs are 70 to 75 percent more efficient than incandescent lights. That efficiency doesn’t lead to lower brightness either, with LEDs actually shining far stronger than most classic bulbs. The LED itself is a semiconductor that emits light when current passes through it. Furthermore, without a delicate filament inside, LEDs are far more durable.

While LEDs in flashlights are more efficient than traditional bulbs, they still generate a fair amount of heat. Especially as brands continue to push to create brighter and brighter flashlights, the heat generated grows too. That noted, most LED flashlights have circuitry designed to manage power consumption and prevent your light from burning up.

For the most part, as long as you use common sense and don’t max out your light for hours on end, your LED flashlight should be fine. Take care of it responsibly and you’ll never deal with heat challenges.

Industry observers note that the actual brightness of your flashlight is measured in lumens. Lumens are essentially measuring the total light created by flashlight, with the higher the figure, the brighter the flashlight should shine.

Even accurate figures reported by a tech giant can often refer to the absolute highest possible lumen output, which is not realistically what you end up using most of the time. Being able to measure them ourselves provides a lot of much needed reassurance.

That noted, lumens aren’t the end all, be all. A lot of the perceived brightness and clarity of the beam is due to the reflector shape and lens. So, the width and length of the light beam from your flashlight will likely be a better determination of whether it works for you or not.

IP is short for ingress protection, meaning protection from stuff getting inside the flashlight. Those letters will be followed by two numbers: The first digit indicates protection from solids like dust or grit. The second digit indicates protection from moisture, in this case the concern is usually water. Sometimes there will be an “X” in place of one of those numbers, which means the flashlight hasn’t been tested for protection from solids (if the X is where the first number should be) or liquids (if it’s where the second should be).

Recent findings suggest that for the first number, protection from solids, the highest rating, 6, indicates the light should be impenetrable by dust and sand. The highest value for the second number, representing protection from liquid, is 8. The flashlight can be submerged in water deeper than 1 meter for longer than 30 minutes, with no harmful effects.

According to recent reports, A flashlight’s IP rating gives a partial picture of its durability. You’ll also want to take into account things like the materials used—ranging from lightweight but less-than-durable plastic to rubberized enclosures to heavy-duty anodized aluminum—and whether the flashlight floats in water in addition to being waterproof, not to mention the warranty.

According to recent reports, as our first-hand testing indicated, manufacturer estimates for flashlight specs are relatively accurate, especially regarding the peak brightness. It’s vital to keep in mind that there are a variety of factors that can influence a flashlight’s moment-to-moment performance, such as its battery life and how long it has run in the past few hours.

Sources indicate that as we mentioned, it is normal for flashlights to only shine at peak brightness for a few minutes before sliding back to the middle of their range. The good news is your visibility won’t suffer for that.

According to recent reports, that depends on how you’re using your flashlight. Manufacturer Nitecore suggests a range of 1 to 300 lumens should be enough to light up a room or an intermittently lit outdoor area. Look for 300 to 980 lumens for walking in the dark without any additional light sources. Mechanics and other workers who need to see precise details in complete darkness might go a little higher, say 1,000 to 1,300 lumens.

In a recent development, hunters or law enforcement might use brighter flashlights than that, but it really depends on the task. Furthermore, it’s crucial to remember that powerful flashlights can be disruptive to other people and wildlife, so choose your light carefully.

Industry observers note that flashlight enthusiasts often recommend making a flash part of your “everyday carry,” keeping it on you at all times as you would with your keys or smartphone. Personally, we recommend being proactive and keeping it around whenever or wherever you think there’s a chance you may need some extra light. For example, if you’re going on a hiking trip or evening walk, it’s a no-brainer.

It’s never a bad idea to stash a flashlight on each floor of your home in case of a power outage or other emergency. That way, you can easily grab it without going up or down stairs in the dark. It’s best to keep them in a place that you know you’ll remember and is easy to find in the dark, such as a small drawer.

We also stronglyrecommend keeping a flashlight in your car, as you never know when you might have a mechanical concern at night, and you’ll want to save your phone battery.

Recent findings suggest that separately, FEMA and The Department of Homeland Security recommend that you keep an emergency kit with a flashlight and other essentials in a cool, dry place somewhere at home, as well as in your car. In order to keep the kit intact and ready for an emergency, the flashlight in your emergency kit should be a backup, not your primary flashlight.

#122949. Australia’s legless geckos evolved like snakes did

Australia’s legless geckos evolved like snakes did

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencenews

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, this is a human-written story voiced by AI.
  • Australia’s limbless geckos look a lot like snakes.
  • In a recent development, snakes are technically a highly modified group of legless lizards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

Australia’s limbless geckos look a lot like snakes. It turns out they’ve evolved like snakes too.

In a recent development, snakes are technically a highly modified group of legless lizards. Dozens of other lizard lineages have independently lost their legs, too. But the legless pygopod geckos aren’t quite like their slithering nonsnake kin. Pygopods have dietary pickiness and physical diversity patterns that are more reminiscent of those found in snakes than in other legless lizards, researchers report in a preprint posted at bioRxiv.org on October 23.

In a recent development, the 50 recognized species of pygopod geckos are found throughout Australia and Newly introduced Guinea. Pygopods range from a meter long to the size of half a cooked spaghetti noodle. They have odd tails, which in some species can be fantastically long, exceeding 400 percent of their less-than-1-centimeter-long bodies. Some use their tails like a spring to leap.

“They create a little sine wave and they shoot themselves up in the air, and they can do successive jumps,” says Ian Brennan, an evolutionary biologist at the Queensland Museum Kurilpa in Brisbane, Australia.

But not much else is known about them, Brennan states.

In a recent development, “They’re real oddballs,” he states, noting that geckos are typically thought of as skilled climbers on walls or glass surfaces. “[Pygopods are] a group that’s gone the exact opposite direction.”.

As part of a large project tackling the genetics of Australia’s lizards and snakes, Brennan and his colleagues gathered data on pygopods’ genes, diet and physical features. They analyzed DNA from all 50 species of pygopod and generated an evolutionary tree. The team also put together data from the literature on the ratio of their body and tail lengths and compared this with a dataset of similar information on over 3,100 lizard and snake species.

As they evolved, snakes got longer by lengthening their bodies. Limbed lizards tend to get longer by lengthening their tails. The team found that pygopods have done both, an unusual strategy among legless lizards. This dual strategy resulted in some unexpected physical diversity in tail and body ratio.

According to recent reports, next, the team tackled diet, comparing between 1,738 lizard and snake species. Snakes as a group have a broad diet with lots of specialization, which might be partly why they’ve been so successful at diversifying into so many ecological roles in so many habitats, Brennan says. There are pythons that eat only large mammals and sea snakes that eat only fish eggs, for instance.

This pattern is rare in lizards. Most geckos eat insects such as beetles and cockroaches, Brennan says. This is especially true of the legless groups, which mostly gobble down whatever insects they happen to slither past.

According to recent reports, but the team found that the wide variety in what pygopods as a group will eat is exceeded among reptiles only by monitor lizards and colubrid snakes, a hyperdiverse group of over 2,000 snake species. Within that broad dietary range, particular pygopods flirt with snakelike pickiness. Some pygopods chiefly hunt spiders and scorpions. Another group targets ants and termites. One predatory pygopod — the Lialis genus — gulps down other lizards snake-style.

Pygopods’ evolutionary history may provide hints about how this heightened diversity developed. The team’s findings suggest they split off from other geckos in Australia 50 million years ago — much more recently than when the first snakes evolved around 160 million years ago, but before any modern snake groups reached Australia. Brennan thinks pygopods filled the roles of small snakes on the continent for millions of years in isolation.

It has been revealed that “Pygopods were probably on a trajectory to do something spectacular, like snakes,” states Brennan. “But then all of these [snake] groups demonstrated up in Australia and filled into those niches.”.

Sonal Singhal — an evolutionary biologist at California State University, Dominguez Hills in Carson — would like to see this study’s data combined with data on pygopods’ skull shape, their habitat use and how their bodies move.

“For example, Lialis can swallow prey whole because their jaws are so flexible and kinetic and their teeth hinge back and forth, allowing them to trap prey.”.

For Brennan, a lesson from the findings is that lacking limbs need not be an evolutionary constraint. Both snakes and pygopods “have diversified to do really interesting things, either due to or in spite of being limbless,” he says.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that instead of driving for every short trip to the store or commute to work, hop on an electric scooter and zoom through your neighborhood. Electric scooters are easier to ride than electric skateboards and more portable than electric bikes, so they’re a great alternative for city-dwellers who don’t have the space for a car or would prefer a smaller mode of transportation for short distances.

These days, there are plenty of affordable and durable electric scooters available. Options range from electric scooters built for just a few miles of daily commuting to ones designed to handle uneven trails, high speeds, and long distances. We tried out electric scooters on our own commutes to find the best.

What Are the Laws for Riding E-Scooters?In many areas, electric scooters aren’t allowed on sidewalks, so check whether you need to ride in bike lanes before you jet around. Some areas have speed limits on small electric vehicles like scooters and e-bikes. For instance, in Florida, e-scooters with seats must be registered and have a title and license plate, so check your local laws before you opt for one of our seated options. Similarly, there are some restrictions based on battery size and type.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a scooter that can do just about everything well—with a long range to boot—check out the Segway Ninebot Kickscooter Max. It can go up to 40 miles on a single charge, handle slopes up to 22 degrees, and carry riders up to 265 pounds.

Its 10-inch pneumatic tires are great at absorbing bumps in the road, and it folds easily for storage. The tires are “self-sealing,” meaning an interior liner will automatically fill in punctures for a short-term patch. It’s not a permanent solution, but even if you roll over a nail or sharp rock, you’ll be able to continue driving without stopping for an immediate replacement. At just over 40 pounds, this Ninebot is heavier than some commuter scooters. But some of that comes from the bigger battery for extended range.

While 40 miles won’t take you on long-range adventures, it should last for multiple weeks of scootering around town. The Ninebot is the second most expensive of the scooters we recommend. But considering how well-rounded this e-scooter is, it’s the best for most people.

It has been revealed that the GoTrax XR Elite needs to be on your radar if you’re looking for an electric scooter that doesn’t take a bite out of your wallet. At just 32 pounds, it’s one of the lightest and easiest to carry among the scooters here. This is further amplified by the foldable design and slender frame.

In a recent development, this scooter has an estimated range of 16 miles, a top speed of about 15 miles per hour, and a max incline of 15 degrees. What really sets it apart from the others is the affordable price given the quality performance. This costs about $400 less than the Segway Ninebot Kickscooter Max.

Sources indicate that while the XR Elite isn’t built for long distances or top speeds, it’s a perfect choice for puttering around town. Moreover, its battery charges in just four hours, allowing you to get around sooner if need be.

According to recent reports, very few electric scooters offer the balance of affordability and performance that the Gotrax G3 Max does. With a maximum range of 37 miles, the scooter is ideal for daily commuting back and forth to work without the constant need to recharge.

Beyond this, the scooter is equipped with a number of features that caught our eye, including the integrated number lock on the body that dissuades thieves by preventing them from actually being able to unfold and ride the scooter without the right code.

The G3 Max also comes with an LED display showing your speed, speed modes, mileage, and battery life. There’s an LED headlight for riding at night too.

Full Gotrax G3 Max Electric Scooter Review.

It has been revealed that don’t confuse this electric scooter with a bike or moped. Built with a seat and basket, the Flex Ultra from Gotrax is more than just a quick commuter.

According to recent reports, when testing this scooter, I took it from Central Park all the way back to my apartment in Brooklyn. I had my backpack, which weighed over 20 pounds, in the basket, and I sat on the seat for the majority of the trip.

Recent findings suggest that what I noticed immediately was the zip of the motor as I got close to 20 miles per hour on straightaways and churned up the incline of the Queensboro Bridge without losing momentum. I also have to admit that I loved the seat. Instead of standing for over 30 minutes on the ride back, I could rest a bit more while still making better time than I would on the subway.

The throttle is responsive, and the larger 14-inch wheels stood up well to the potholes on the streets and cracks on the pavement. While its size prevents it from being an easy storage item in a closet—even though it folds—this electric scooter comes with the power, comfort, and convenience for quick grocery trips and long city commutes alike.

Industry observers note that with a 34-mile range and a top speed of 20 miles per hour, the Ninebot E3 Pro is an ideal commuter scooter balancing speed and range. It’s also quite durable, with an alloy frame boasting an IPX5 water resistance for riding through puddles, rain, and even mud.

Industry observers note that furthermore, the electric scooter is a relatively quick charge, going from zero to fully charged in 7 hours. This means you can plug it in overnight and ride out in the morning on a full charge with no worry. Alongside an LED headlight, the scooter comes with lighting underneath the board so you’ll have full visibility at night.

The headlight and under-board lighting are paired with real turn signals as well, so you don’t have to take your hands of the handles to let drivers around you know which direction you’re headed.

Full Segway E3 Pro Electric Scooter Review.

Recent findings suggest that this lightweight and affordable scooter won’t take you everywhere with just a 16 mile range, but you can take it anywhere you please. The scooter is small enough to fold up and carry without feeling like it’s dragging on your arm after a few minutes.

While it won’t exactly disappear under a desk, it’s probably one of the few that will fit with ease in a storage closet or under the bed at home. At the same time, you can toss it in the back of your trunk and take it out whenever you go to the park.

The hollow tires also mean you’ll never run flat and don’t need to worry about inflating them after a few winter months out of use.

It has been revealed that have you ever wanted to take a load off while riding but don’t want a permanent seat? The Gotrax Eclipse offers the best of both worlds. The electric scooter comes with a detachable seat so you can plop down if you know you have a long ride ahead, but can take it off and leave it at home when portability and foldability take priority.

Industry observers note that the scooter is more than just the seat as well. With a top speed of 25 miles per hour and a max range of 38 miles, this is a performance-focused option that is great for longer commutes and open streets.

At the same time, the electric scooter has a small rear shelf that can be used to securely tie down small packages and backpacks so you can actually use it for carrying more than just yourself.

Reaching speeds of over 30 miles per hour and boasting a range of 45, this electric scooter from Segway is aptly named the SuperScooter GT3. This heavy-duty option is designed with performance as the end all, be all priority. In fact, in combination with its 11-inch self-sealing tires, the SuperScooter GT3 is one of the few electric scooters that is legitimately well-equipped to handle gravel, dirt, and general off-road adventures.

Recent findings suggest that beyond pure power and battery, the electric scooter comes with one of the most useful displays that we’ve found. The full color screen comes with smart technology that connects to your phone so you can receive notifications and access navigation routes in real time.

That said, before you click buy, make sure it’s actually legal to ride in your city. Electric scooters of this speed and size are often highly regulated and illegal to ride in densely populated cities across the United States.

An electric scooter’s range is based on battery and motor size and is impacted by a number of factors, including rider weight, weather conditions, surface type, and incline of the roads you travel on. The ranges we include are based on the manufacturers’ claims, and your real-world use will vary.

Recent findings suggest that many scooters get up to 10 miles, while some can last for up to 40 miles or more on a single charge. Some have various drive settings that help you get the most juice out of your battery based on the type of ride you’re on. For instance, if you’re trying to conserve power for a longer trip, many options have a low-power or eco mode, which reduces top speed or acceleration for the sake of saving the battery. Furthermore, if you want to extend your scooter range as much as possible, consider routing yourself on smooth flat roads with little incline that don't require lots of stopping and starting.

It has been revealed that most of the e-scooters we recommend top out between 15 and 20 mph. That should be fast enough to zip along city streets and paths without feeling like you’re falling behind.

The only exception to this speed range is the Navee XT5 electric scooter, which reaches a top speed of 31 mph. However, if you’re seeking a quicker commute or more of a thrill, there are other e-scooters that reach speeds up to 60 mph. We didn’t recommend any of those because many states and cities have banned them or require you to gain an additional license to use them.

In a recent development, electric scooters often have motors with a power rating between 250 and 350 watts. This is enough for most daily city commuting. If you’re a heavier person or expected to ride up steep inclines, you may want to opt for a scooter with a larger, more powerful motor. High wattage motors offer significantly more torque and acceleration but typically come at a premium. Their size also makes them heavier than lower wattage motors, which can make the scooter more cumbersome to carry or transport when not in use.

Almost all electric scooters have rubber tires, whether they’re solid, tubeless, or tires with inner tubes. Solid rubber tires are the longest-lasting and are ideal for those making shorter rides on smooth streets, but they also absorb less shock than their tubeless counterparts.

Tires with inner tubes were more common in the past, but we’re starting to see more tubeless and tube-ready tires today. Both tubeless and tube-ready tires can suffer punctures, but offer more cushioning during a ride than solid rubber models.

If you proposal on riding a scooter in the early morning or night, look for a scooter with good front and rear lights. It’s also a good idea to look for a scooter with a horn or bell to warn bikers, pedestrians, and other scooter riders that you’re approaching. Some high end scooters also come with board lights and turn signals for additional visibility in the dark.

All scooters should have good brakes as well. Some only have them on one wheel, but more powerful scooters that need to decelerate rapidly should have front and back brakes, and possibly a motor brake so you don’t go flying down a hill faster than intended. Motor brakes can also provide some regenerative braking, extending the scooter’s range slightly as you ride.

According to recent reports, some other extras to look for on electric scooters are items like seats or baskets. These are great to have if you prefer a seated ride and/or if you initiative on using the scooter for errands, like grocery shopping.

Recent findings suggest that in selecting these electric scooters, we rode multiple options. We used the scooters in daily work commutes to test their power, speed, range, and comfort over distance. This included trips over long bridges, on steep inclines, and many times, on streets without bike lanes. We also gauged how the acceleration and brakes felt in our hands, and how smooth the scooter stayed when riding over bumps or uneven asphalt.

For scooters we haven’t tested yet, we based our picks on research, evaluating the opinions and ratings of professional reviewers, as well as checking out customer reviews and rankings, and evaluating each model’s most important specs like wattage, range, and safety features. We chose reputable brands, selecting electric scooters that are not only the highest-performing models on the market, but also the easiest to find in stock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

When astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day. But scientists soon realized this one was something very special, and they’ve been hustling to study it ever since.

“I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” says astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University.

It has been revealed that soon after scientists spotted the explosion on November 2, they determined it hadn’t yet peaked in brightness, giving scientists an early glimpse at the event. Even more thrilling, within a day of the explosion’s discovery, astronomers had classified it as a type Ia supernova. These particular outbursts are rare, but they’re astronomical superstars: Scientists use their trademark explosion pattern as a “standard candle” to measure distance into the universe — most notably to discover that the universe’s expansion is accelerating. And to round out a trifecta of reasons to be excited, these blasts rarely occur so close to Earth.

Astronomers know type 1a supernovas occur upon the reignition and resulting self-destruction of a white dwarf star, the small cool remnants of a star like the sun that’s too small to become a superdense neutron star or black hole at its demise. Scientists also know that powering back on requires reaching about 1.44 times the mass of the sun, which can occur only if something is giving the white dwarf extra mass.

But scientists aren’t sure what that something is — whether these supernovas are triggered by a second white dwarf or some sort of star that’s still burning. Usually, these explosions occur so far away that astronomers can’t get a good look at where they come from. But SN 2026ahvu is perhaps 50 million light-years or less away from Earth.

“They happen so rarely at this distance that it could hopefully help us figure out why this white dwarf exploded in the first place,” states astronomer Yvette Cendes of the University of Oregon in Eugene, who has been arranging for radio telescopes to observe the outburst.

Sources indicate that sarbadhicary and colleagues have already submitted preliminary findings November 6 at arXiv.org suggesting that the former white dwarf was less than 100 million years old. That’s remarkably young compared with other supernovas of this type, and may help scientists finetune their understanding of these outbursts.

“These explosions have been enduring mysteries for us for decades, and whenever something happens this close, it’s just really exciting,” Sarbadhicary says.

The primary legislative business this week is the Senate's bipartisan permitting overhaul, but a late-breaking aviation funding fight and the Senate Democratic leadership contest are also commanding attention.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., last week formally introduced a leadership challenge to Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., and both men are accumulating supporters ahead of leadership votes that are at the moment scheduled for early December — though there's been an effort to move that up to this week.

Van Hollen has expressed disagreement with Schumer's participation in primaries.

That's going to be one of several flash points for December's funding discussions, as President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans try to use what leverage they have before Democrats take the gavels in the House and the Senate in January.

It has been revealed that sen. The 7 Best Portable Jump Starters to Bring Your Vehicle Back to Life

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Sources indicate that if you’ve got a dead car battery, you’ll want the option to revive it without waiting for help.
  • A portable jump starter, which is a compact and powerful battery consisting of lightweight lithium-ion, is a handy device that’s faster, safer, and more convenient than jumper cables because you don’t need to find another car with a willing driver.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that if you’ve got a dead car battery, you’ll want the option to revive it without waiting for help. According to AAA’s most recent report, of the 27 million calls received across the country for roadside assistance, 7 million of those vehicles had battery trouble. The causes may include anything from neglecting to turn off your car’s ignition or headlights, residing in an extremely cold climate, or even a slowly deteriorating alternator.

A portable jump starter, which is a compact and powerful battery consisting of lightweight lithium-ion, is a handy device that’s faster, safer, and more convenient than jumper cables because you don’t need to find another car with a willing driver.

Like all batteries, lithium-ion cells have different power ratings and can become depleted from repeated use or by sitting idle over time. That’s why before purchasing a portable jump starter, consider these two specs: peak amperage (amps) which conveys how much power a device can deliver, and capacity (rated in milliampere-hours, mAh), indicating how long a device can hold a charge when stored and still have enough power to provide a jump. It’s also important to monitor the charge level on your portable jump starter from time to time. I do this regularly while waiting to fill my gas tank.

In a recent development, there are other convenience features these devices offer, like USB ports to recharge portable electronics and lights for illumination when it’s dark. Many portable jump starters have what’s called a boost button, which I recommend having, as it supplies extra momentary power for severely drained batteries. After several rounds of testing, research, and evaluation, these are the top portable jump starters to buy now.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve owned close to a dozen vehicles during my 30-year-plus career writing about cars and have had plenty of dead batteries. I keep jumper cables in each of my three current vehicles, and now I also have a portable jump starter on board along with a portable tire inflator, dash cam, and Cobra RAD 700i radar detector, which I move between vehicles depending on which I decide to drive.

Industry observers note that in short, each device in this roundup can promptly start a vehicle with a depleted battery. While testing each product, I also evaluated its peak instantaneous power measured in amps, power capacity measured in milliampere-hours, the quantity and variety of output ports to charge portable electronics, and extras such as lights and a boost button.

In a recent development, my recommendations are based on a product’s price, capability, and capacity to fit a wide array of vehicles and budgets. I took into account my own experiences with portable jump starters, each brand’s reputation, and for further background, I spoke with fellow car enthusiasts and auto journalists to get their impressions.

Industry observers note that with 6,000-amp peak current to jump-start a vehicle with up to a 12.0-liter diesel engine coupled with 27,000 mAh of power capacity, the Gooloo GT6000 is the most powerful device in our guide. The GT6000 offers up to 24 months of standby time—and with that, you get incredible peace of mind. This device can sit unused for long stretches and still be counted on to crank your car when needed. If its battery is depleted, the GT6000 is ready to jump-start a vehicle after just 7 minutes of recharging and is fully recharged in 1.4 hours via its 100-watt USB-C in/out port.

In a recent development, this device also stands out for its generous quantity and variety of charging ports. In addition to a 100-watt USB-C in/out port, it also has a 12-volt/cigarette-lighter cord to recharge its battery in a pinch. A 15 volt/10-amp DC port can be used to power assorted car accessories like portable air pumps and power inverters. There are two USB-A power ports, one rated at 5-volts/2.4-amps and another rated for 5/9/12-volts.

It has been revealed that the GT6000 is one of only two devices here with an LCD screen, which makes checking battery level, charging output, temperature, and jump-start status quick and easy. There are 10 safety features, in addition to a built-in LED flashlight with three lighting modes (flashlight, strobe, and SOS) that provides illumination when using the device in low-light situations—key so other motorists can see you if you’re stuck on the side of the road.

While the GT6000 admittedly provides more power than most motorists will likely need, and it’s one of the heaviest of our picks, it is without question the best overall jump starter for maximum instantaneous power, long standby time, quick recharging, and plenty of output ports.

The AstroAI S8 isn’t the most powerful jump-starter recommended but it’s one of the lowest-priced and is user friendly and small enough to fit in your car’s glove box or map pocket. Although it taps out on vehicles with anything larger than a 6.0-liter gas or 3.0-liter diesel engine, it’s fine for most vehicles. I’ve kept this in one of my vehicles for months and used it several times to provide jump-starts to others without an glitch.

Protection against reverse polarity, overcurrent, overvoltage, overload, overcharge, over discharge, and short circuiting are built in. The AstroAI S8 has two 5-volt/2.4-amp USB-A output ports to charge portable devices and an LED flashlight with normal, strobe, and SOS modes. It is supplied with a USB A to USB C charging cable to recharge the device.

The interface is one of the most barebones of all the units tested—just a power button and four blue LEDs to indicate power level. It does have a boost button but is the only unit of our selections without a shut-off switch; instead it automatically powers off after 30 seconds.Full AstroAI S8 Portable Jump Starter Review.

This is the smallest device I tested (only slightly larger than most smartphones) and the lightest at 1.2 pounds. With 2,000 amps of peak power, the Gooloo GP2000 can jump-start vehicles with up to 8.0-liter gas or 6.0-liter diesel engines and its 12,000 mAh of capacity is impressive for its size and price.

It has 10 safety protection features including short circuit and reverse polarity, and a 400-lumen LED flashlight with normal, strobe, and SOS modes to provide light in dark environments and during emergency roadside stops. It comes with two USB-A outputs—one 5/9/12-volt and one 5-volt/2.4-amp—for charging portable devices, a USB-C charging cable, and a storage case instead of a bag like many portable jump starters at this price.

According to recent reports, like the AstroAI S8, it has only an on-off button. It’s easy to use and has a boost button. I recommend this option for anyone looking for a small, inexpensive, and hassle-free portable jump starter.

With an IP65 water-resistance rating and rubberized casing, the Noco Boost Plus is the portable jump starter I turn to during the rainy season in Oregon—which means anytime other than summer. I go for this one because it has spark-proof and reverse polarity protection for safe use in wet or dry conditions.

In a recent development, its 1,000-amp peak power rating can start vehicles with up to 6.0-liter gas and 3.0-liter diesel engines. However, its 2,150 mAh capacity is the lowest of any product here, so it may not hold a charge as long as jump starters with a higher capacity. While this is adequate, I don’t recommend a mAh rating any lower.

Sources indicate that the Noco GB40’s 100-lumen flashlight is dimmer than that of some of the other units in this roundup but it has the most modes, six total, which include 100-, 50-, and 10 percent; blink, SOS, and strobe. It also comes with a 1-foot USB-C charging cable, but it has only one 5-volt/2.1-amp USB-A output port for charging your portable electronics.

Full Noco GB40 Boost Plus Review.

If you own a large vehicle, the Noco Boost X GBX155 cranks out 4,250 amps to boost batteries instantaneously for vehicles with up to 10.0-liter gas and 8.0-liter diesel engines, and has an impressive 26,750 mAh capacity, just shy of the Gooloo GT6000’s 27,000-mAh spec. A 60-watt USB-C input/output allows recharging from 0-to-100 percent capacity in 2.7 hours to ensure it’s ready to jump-start a vehicle after charging only 5 minutes (slightly faster than the Gooloo GT6000’s 7 minutes.).

I found the Noco Boost X GBX155 more complicated to operate than the other portable jump starters I tested. For example, it doesn’t have a boost button like other units but rather a manual override feature that’s used to jump start severely depleted batteries if the device detects the battery is below 3 volts. Aactivating the feature requires holding the Manual Override button for 3 seconds, which can send the GBX155’s maximum output of 4,250 amps to jump start a vehicle. This Manual Override shuts off the Noco’s automatic spark-proof and reverse-polarity protection so people need to be extra careful to attach the jumper cables correctly (red to positive, black to negative) to avoid damaging the car’s electrical system, and not touch the clamps together, which can create dangerous sparking.

According to recent reports, the Noco is heavy, too, at 5.8 pounds. In addition to its 60-watt USB-C input/output, it has only one 5-volt/2.1-amp USB-A port whereas other lower-priced devices have at least two. But you won’t be working in the dark if you are trying to start your battery at night. This device has a 500-lumen LED flashlight that’s the brightest of the portable jump starters in our roundup. Another perk: it’s got an IP65 waterproof rating (with its input/output ports covered) that only the Gooloo GT6000 and Noco GB40 also have.

Industry observers note that for motorheads with multiple vehicles and a garage or shop to keep them, the Clore Automotive Jump-N-Carry JNC660 is a worthy device to have on hand. Its 120-volt male receptacle connects to an extension cord so that it can be powered by a regular wall outlet and is always charged and ready.

This device uses a lead-acid battery instead of a lithium-ion one. This makes the battery replaceable, so this device is not ultimately disposable like portable jump starters with a lithium-ion battery. At 18 pounds, it’s by far the heaviest here, but also has the longest (46 inches) and thickest (2-gauge) jumper cables.

With 1,700 peak amps, it’s not the most powerful portable jump starter included but makes up for that with a 22,000 mAh rating which means its internal battery holds a charge longer. A built-in digital voltmeter reveals the battery’s state of charge before and after a jump start and it has a DC outlet to power 12-volt accessories such as a tire inflator or power inverter. A notable drawback: It doesn’t have USB output ports.

Recent findings suggest that for years, I relied on a Battery Tender trickle charger to supply a slow, steady current to keep the battery in my classic Chevy Impala SS charged. If you also have a vehicle that sits idle for months on end, check out the Battery Tender Charge N Start 4120. It does double duty as a trickle charger and a jump starter. However, combining two devices in one comes with compromises such as not having output ports to charge portable devices, or a boost button.

With 1,200 amps of instantaneous current, this device can jump start cars with up to 6.0-liter gas or 4.0-liter diesel engines and proficiently cranked the engine on several large and small vehicles during my testing. Its basic push-button interface makes the Charge N Start a breeze to operate. Safety features include spark-proof connection, reverse-polarity protection, and more.

This portable jump starter sends a small amount of current to traditional lead-acid as well as lithium batteries at 4 amps, and an onboard microprocessor maintains the optimal voltage to keep a battery at 100-percent capacity without overcharging during long-term storage. It also includes temperature compensation to handle a range of climates.

Something you may need to think about is its size. Its larger than other trickle chargers I’ve used, which affects placement. Ideally, a trickle charger should be located close to the battery under a car’s hood. The Charge N Start may be too large to tuck away under the closed hood of certain vehicles, but a supplied 6-foot extension cable that attaches to low-profile battery-charging clamps allows locating the device away from the engine on, say, a shelf next to a wall outlet.

The Noco AX65 is another portable jump starter we’ve tested and recommend, but we moved it out of our guide because it’s not singularly a portable jump starter like the others. This is a combo device with a portable air compressor so you can start dead batteries and inflate flat tires. What I like is that the unit doesn’t skimp on either function. The jump starter has an impressive 16,000 mAh capacity and delivers 2,000 amps of peak power while the tire inflator pumps out 67 liters per minute of airflow, which converts to 2.3 cubic feet per minute (cfm)—well above average for the portable tire inflators I’ve tested.

The portable jump starter can crank a dead battery on vehicles with gas engines as large as 8.0 liters and diesel engines up to 6.0 liters. It can be used for SUVs, boats, and snowmobiles. The not-so-good news: It’s short on output ports compared to the other portable jump starters here, and heavy at more than 9 pounds.

Portable jump starters are essentially heavy-duty batteries that come with jumper cables, controls, and accessories like lights, charging ports, and air pumps. Here’s what to look for when shopping for a portable jump starter that fits your vehicle, needs, and budget.

Recent findings suggest that the two most important specs to look for when comparing portable jump starters are peak amperes (amps) and milliampere-hours (mAh). Peak amps indicate the maximum short-term current a device can deliver, while mAh measures how much electrical charge a battery can store.

Bigger is better for both specs, although mAh isn’t always as prominent or even stated with portable jump starters compared to peak amps. About 400 to 600 peak amps is sufficient to jump-start vehicles like cars and crossovers, although large SUVs, trucks, RVs, and commercial vehicles may require up to 1,500 or 2,000 amps. Some portable jump starters come with a boost button that provides roughly 10 additional amps and is helpful when reviving a very dead battery that needs an extra jolt of juice. At least 10,000 mAh of capacity means the battery in a portable jump starter will hold enough charge for 3 to 6 months to deliver 5 to 10 jump-starts.

Portable jump starters are a much safer alternative to using jumper cables to revive a dead battery because connecting jumper cables to a battery’s terminals can cause sparks that can sometimes ignite gas produced by the battery and cause an explosion. Also, if you connect the cables incorrectly, called reverse polarity, it can severely damage a car’s electrical system. Unlike jumper cables, portable jump starters have built-in protection against issues like sparking and reverse polarity in addition to other safety features and are much less risky and easier to use.

Most portable jump starters also come in handy for recharging phones, tablets, and other portable devices. USB output ports are the most common, but a few devices also provide a 12-volt outlet. While USB ports typically charge at 2.5 to 5 volts, a 12-volt outlet can not only charge a device faster but can also be used to power devices such as portable air pumps and coolers.

If you need to jump-start a vehicle at night, you’ll be thankful your portable jump starter has an LED flashlight. Typically a portable jump starter’s lighting feature also provides strobe or SOS patterns to warn other motorists on the road of your presence.

In a recent development, look for a portable jump starter with a boost button to give an extra jolt of juice to a very depleted battery when the device’s standard output can’t crank the engine. This surge of power gives you about 15 to 30 seconds to start the car once the boost button is pressed.

In a recent development, A portable jump starter rated for 400 to 600 amps is sufficient to jump-start most passenger vehicles such as cars, crossovers, and smaller SUVs. But for larger SUVs, trucks, RVs, and commercial vehicles you want to look for a device with at least 1,500 to 2,000 amps. Weather also affects a car battery and engine, so if you live in a very cold climate more power may be needed to jump-start a low or dead battery.

Sources indicate that yes and no since it depends on the wide range of passenger vehicles available. A portable jump starter with a lower amp rating can jump-start smaller vehicles such as most cars, crossovers, and small SUVs. But a large SUV or truck with a large engine will require a portable jump starter with a higher amp rating.

According to recent reports, peak power rating (measured in amps) to ensure a portable jump starter has enough juice to crank your vehicle and capacity (measured in milliamp hours) that indicates how long it can potentially hold a charge are the most two important. Other features to look for include the number and types of output charging ports, whether it has a 12-volt output and charging input, a boost button, and a flashlight.

Sources indicate that definitely. Make sure to first read the owner’s manual to understand how your portable jump starter works before connecting it to a car’s battery. When using it, take off any jewelry and wear safety glasses and gloves anytime you work on a vehicle and especially around a battery. Most portable jump starters come with built-in safety features that will issue a warning if they are connected incorrectly. But it’s up to you to double-check that the jump starter’s red/positive and black/negative clamps are connected to the (typically) red positive and black negative terminals of the car battery.

Recent findings suggest that yes, a portable jump starter is a much safer alternative to using traditional jumper cables to start a vehicle with a dead battery. Connecting jumper cables to a battery’s terminals can cause sparks that have the potential to ignite gas produced by a battery which in some instances can lead to an explosion. And if you connect the cables incorrectly (in reverse polarity) it can severely damage a car’s electrical system. Unlike jumper cables, most portable jump starters come with built-in protection against complications like sparking and reverse polarity and are much less risky and easier to use. Plus, with a portable jump starter you don’t have to find another car—and a driver—like you do with jump cables. That remarked, I carry a set of jumper cables as a backup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silversea has unveiled a series of enhancements onboard the Silver Dawn following its recent drydock in Genoa.

They include the addition of Riviera, a latest poolside dining, bar and lounge concept first introduced on the Silver Spirit earlier this year, as well as new outdoor experiences.

The firm describes Riviera as an open-air concept that is part restaurant, part bar where guests can enjoy drinks, fresh seafood and a mix of daily activities, from morning yoga to evening soirées.

“Silver Dawn’s enhancements reflect our commitment to bringing more options to guests across our fleet,” said Bert Hernandez, president, Silversea.

According to recent reports, “With the expansion of Riviera and the addition new outdoor sports, guests have greater variety in how they spend their time onboard. As Silver Dawn sails the Mediterranean and the Caribbean in the coming seasons, guests will find that choice alongside the personalized service that defines Silversea.”.

The Riviera concept brings a significant upgrade to the ship’s outdoor guest spaces, bringing new cabanas, loungers, umbrellas, ambient lighting and refreshed furniture layouts.

Guests will also be able to enjoy outdoor sports, with the ship getting three outdoor recreation spaces – a pickleball court, a golf putting area and a golf hitting bay.

The Silver Dawn will welcome its first passengers after drydock on November 25, 2026, a 14-day sailing from Civitavecchia (Rome) to Lisbon through the Mediterranean.

The voyage calls at 10 ports across Italy, Malta, Tunisia, Spain, and Portugal, including Naples, Valletta, Trapani in Sicily, Tunis, Cagliari in Sardinia, Cartagena, Malaga and Cádiz, with overnights in Valletta and Malaga.

#122940. The 7 Best Pocket Knives for Everyday Tasks and Outdoor Adventures
